confirmed.claim: receipt.json, calls.jsonl and rejections.jsonl are written only when run() returns normally; CALLS and REJECTIONS live in memory, so any death of the session before the last document loses every per-call model/tokens/latency row (a BUILD.md rule) and every schema rejection.
confirmed.scenario: The sample is ~2,600 sequential derive calls plus judge, fold and embed calls with no concurrency; if the average call is 10 to 15 s the run is 8 to 12 h, at the edge of Kaggle's session limit. When Kaggle kills the kernel (or an exception escapes from load_document/completed/show at lines 1044, 1045, 1060, which sit outside the try, or the user stops the session), packages, ingest.log and manifest.jsonl survive but calls.jsonl, rejections.jsonl and receipt.json are never written. On the next session receipt() reports cost 0 and calls 0 for those documents because it sums the in-memory CALLS, so the real per-call cost/latency record for the money spent is unrecoverable.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reading the code and by a stubbed reproduction. CALLS and REJECTIONS are only ever appended in memory (lines 184, 201, 222 of notebooks/factledger-ingestor.py) and reach disk only inside receipt() (lines 1094-1096), which block 12 calls once, after run() returns (line 1149). run() catches Exception per document (line 1053) but KeyboardInterrupt (an interactive stop), a kernel kill, and anything raised by load_document/completed/show (lines 1044, 1045, 1060, outside the try) all escape before receipt() runs. Reproduction (exec of the notebook blocks with the test battery's scripted model, cost forced to $0.001/call): session 1 ingested oz/01_55 (82 calls, $0.082) and was interrupted on the second document; OUT held ingest.log, manifest.jsonl and oz/01_55.jsonl, while calls.jsonl, rejections.jsonl and receipt.json were MISSING and the 82 rows were gone. Session 2 in a fresh process on the same OUT skipped oz/01_55, ingested one LongMemEval session, and receipt.json then said documents 2, cost 0.004, calls 4, against a manifest sum of $0.086 for the same two documents. Two things the finding understates: (a) it is not only abnormal ends; line 1095 uses write_text, so any resumed session (the designed SpendStop-then-resume flow) overwrites the previous session's calls.jsonl and rejections.jsonl even when both sessions end normally; (b) schema rejections exist nowhere but REJECTIONS (the package's rejection records at lines 963-966 are the semantic ones), so they are lost outright. One thing it overstates: per-document call count and cost survive in each completion record's stats and in manifest.jsonl, so the money spent is recoverable at document granularity; what is unrecoverable is the per-call stage/model/tokens/latency record that BUILD.md ("every call records its model id, tokens, and latency") and the audit's pending tier-spread analysis depend on. Kaggle nuance: if a Save & Run All is killed at the session limit the version's output may not be kept at all, so the fix mainly protects interactive stops, escaped exceptions and multi-session resumes; the receipt-understates-cost defect applies to every resume. Major: a project rule's record is silently lost and receipt.json misreports cost after any resume; the packages themselves are intact and no money is wasted.
confirmed.fix: Persist rows as they are made and derive the receipt from disk: add a small helper in block 2, e.g. `def record(name, row): (OUT / name).open("a", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")` and call it right after each of the three appends (line 184 and 201 for calls.jsonl, line 222 for rejections.jsonl); in receipt() compute cost, calls and calls_by_stage by reading OUT/calls.jsonl instead of CALLS, and delete lines 1095-1096 so a resumed session no longer overwrites earlier rows. Also wrap the run in block 12 as `try: run(uris)` / `finally: print(json.dumps(receipt(), indent=1)[:3000])` so receipt.json is written on an interrupted or errored run too.

Only RUN="all" on the two 2.1 MB Greek histories (142 and 136 units, ~15k chars per unit, plausibly 1,500-2,000 document entities) brings the 300k cap into range. Real defect, remote trigger for the planned run, cheap fix.

confirmed.claim: The retry tuple catches URLError, TimeoutError and OSError, but http.client.IncompleteRead (raised by r.read() in post() when the connection drops mid-body) is an HTTPException, not an OSError, so a truncated response body is neither retried nor counted as spent; it propagates as an unhandled exception and aborts the document.
confirmed.scenario: A 200 reply for a facts call on a 20k-token unit is cut off by a network hiccup on Kaggle after the headers arrive. post() raises http.client.IncompleteRead; line 183 does not match it (verified: issubclass(http.client.IncompleteRead, OSError) is False); call() re-raises, no CALLS row is written for the billed request, run() logs ERROR IncompleteRead and moves on, and the document's preceding calls are lost.
confirmed.what_happens: Confirmed by reproduction. Exec'ing blocks 1-3 the way test_ingestor.py does and stubbing post() to raise http.client.IncompleteRead: call() raises after ONE post with ZERO CALLS rows (no retry, no estimated cost), whereas the same stub raising http.client.RemoteDisconnected (an OSError) gets three attempts and three CALLS rows. IncompleteRead's MRO is HTTPException -> Exception, so the tuple on line 183 cannot match it. In run() the exception falls into the generic `except Exception` (line 1053): the document is logged as ERROR, no package or manifest row is written, and the next run re-derives it from scratch (completed() is false), so the money already spent on that document's earlier calls buys nothing; the truncated-but-billed call itself is absent from CALLS and the receipt. Two mitigating facts keep this at minor: (a) it is rare on a non-streaming chat-completions reply (the body is a few KB sent after generation finishes; socket timeouts, resets and SSL errors during read are all OSError and are caught), and (b) the notebook already accepts an unlogged billed call for other terminal failures (non-200 on line 196, third 429/5xx on line 192), so it is not a new violation of a project rule; BUILD.md and the brief only mandate the schema-retry policy, not transport retries. The scenario as stated is accurate; the phrase "preceding calls are lost" means their work is lost (rows stay in CALLS, so spend accounting for them is intact).
confirmed.fix: Add `import http.client` next to the urllib imports (line 111) and change line 183 to `except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError, http.client.HTTPException):` so a truncated body takes the same estimated-cost, sleep-and-retry path as a timeout.

refuted.claim: On the normalised path, a match that begins or ends inside a character that NFKC or casefold expanded to several characters (a ligature, a sharp s) maps back to the whole original character, so text[start:end] is longer than the model's quote and no longer normalises to it.
refuted.why: The mechanics reproduce exactly as described (exec'ing Block 4 from factledger-ingestor.py: locate('the ﬁrst of them', 'the f') stores 'the ﬁ'; locate('Die Straße ist lang.', 'strass') stores 'Straß'; locate('He left… then', 'He left.') stores 'He left…'), but none of this is a defect against any rule the project states. What is stored is `quote = text[start:end]` (line 529), so quote_start/quote_end slice to exactly the stored quote and the quote lies inside its unit, which is the whole of what SCHEMA.md ("verbatim quote that must appear in its unit, and the offsets where it was found"), the brief (line 75: normalise "for matching only; the stored offsets index the original text"; line 146: offsets slice "to exactly its quote") and the audit promise. Nothing in the contract or the code requires the stored quote to normalise equal to the model's string; the whitespace path already stores a slice that differs from the model's quote (different whitespace), so storing code's verbatim slice rather than the model's text is the established design, not an accident. The widening only occurs when the model's quote boundary falls inside a single original character whose NFKC/casefold expansion is longer (half a ligature, half of ß, a period standing for '…'), and in each case the widened slice is the correct verbatim text of the document that supports the fact, arguably better than the model's approximation. Downstream nothing re-normalises the stored quote against the model's; the fact record is built from `quote`, `quote_start`, `quote_end` only (lines 529-534, 927-928). The proposed fix would turn these matches into 'paraphrase'/'not_found' rejections and drop a fact whose supporting text is genuinely present, which is a worse outcome than a one-character-wider verbatim quote. At most this is a cosmetic remark for the comment at line 285, not a failure scenario.
